requirements_kept: autoReplay stays true; the first publish is still before addSubscriber and the second after it; subscriber count is still asserted to be 1

two distinct payloads so the two messages are distinguishable, both received through the channel under a deadline, content and order asserted, and two different event ids required so a double delivery of one event cannot pass

after both are consumed the empty-queue check remains, then s.close() and the shutdown is observed on the connection itself within a deadline, with an extra message after close reported as a failure; close() returning is never treated as the goroutine having exited

the len assertion was not relaxed to allow 1, no sleep-only or Eventually-empty-queue substitute, the first message was not removed, replay was not disabled, received data was not discarded, and no retry-until-green loop exists

openapi_tail.why: the earlier matrix row B was honest that a direct gow api wrote back the pre-finalize document and needed make openapi afterwards, so the two entries were not equal in their final artifacts
openapi_tail.change: finalizeOpenAPI runs the repository's existing scripts/finalize-aksk-openapi.py inside the staged copy after the template walk and before syncBack; stagingInputs() now names both scripts the chain runs; make api no longer wraps make openapi
openapi_tail.no_duplicate_and_no_recursion: the finalize script is not idempotent by design - it removes one synthetic 200 response and raises SystemExit if that response is already gone - so an outer make openapi after a successful gow api would fail an otherwise good build; that property is pinned by TestFinalOpenApiDocumentIsNotIdempotent (a refused run also leaves the document byte-identical)
tests_added: TestFinalizeOpenAPIRunsInsideTheStagedCopy (marker proves it runs with the stage as cwd and writes nothing into the repository; a stage without the script fails instead of skipping)
